reviewer_ref_note: The reviewer action is pinned to an exact commit SHA, not a branch or a tag. Anything landing on the reviewer's main branch after this commit therefore cannot execute here: the reviewer runs with secrets.GH_PAT (repo scope), secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN, OPENCODE_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY, so an unreviewed upstream push would otherwise acquire duoport's write-capable credentials without any change to this repository. A commit SHA is used rather than a release tag because a tag can be moved or deleted by anyone with release rights, whereas a commit SHA cannot be re-pointed; the ref is content-addressed and reproducible, so every run of these workflows resolves to byte-identical reviewer code. Manual bump procedure: (1) choose the reviewer commit deliberately - a reviewed commit on the reviewer's main branch whose CI, Release and CodeQL runs all conclude success; (2) update reviewer_ref here to that full 40-character SHA and leave reviewer_ref_kind as commit-sha; (3) update all four `uses: nilesh32236/opencode-ai-reviewer@<sha>` references, which are ai-review.yml (three jobs) and daily-audit.yml (one job), keeping the trailing base-version comment accurate; (4) run `php .github/scripts/verify-reviewer-dependency.php`, which fails closed unless the manifest ref is a lowercase 40-character hex SHA, reviewer_ref_kind is commit-sha, and all four references match the manifest exactly. A bump is a reviewed, deliberate act: it is never automatic, never driven by an upstream push, and the pull request carrying it must show the reviewer diff that the previous pin excluded. The OpenCode CLI checksum and merge gate below remain pinned and verified.
